# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a green light, display `0`, and five wires in this order: red, yellow, green, white, blue. I am establishing the required shared gesture code before any operation: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. The blind monkey should wait for the manual’s instructions after this code is established.

``` 
speak(text="I establish the gesture code: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised hand means HOLD, and OK sign means DONE. Everyone wait until the code is established.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s thumbs-up confirms the basic code. Since I can see the bomb but cannot read the manual, I am expanding the gesture code so Mute can relay the manual’s required physical operation. The five wire gestures identify wires 1–5; operation gestures identify what Blind must do. I ask Mute to send the verdict as a gesture sequence, ending with DONE.

``` 
speak(text="Mute, report the manual verdict using gestures. Wire 1 is index-up, wire 2 is index-down, wire 3 is index-left, wire 4 is index-right, and wire 5 is the rightward hand. The pinch gesture means CUT, the small-pinch gesture means PRESS, the heart-hands gesture means TURN, and the horns gesture means PULL. Send the operation followed by its wire number if applicable, then DONE. Use HOLD if more code is needed. Blind, wait for my spoken order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute sent the established HOLD signal. I therefore infer that the manual’s current instruction is to hold, with no wire or control operation specified. I relay that instruction to Blind and do not expand the code because the message fit the existing vocabulary.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not touch or operate anything.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new signal has arrived. The last confirmed manual report was HOLD, so the safe instruction remains to keep the bomb untouched and wait rather than attempt a wire or control operation.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No change: HOLD. Keep all controls and wires untouched.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again sent the established HOLD signal. Nothing on the bomb has changed, so Blind must continue waiting without touching the wires or controls.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD again. Do not touch or operate anything; wait for a new manual instruction.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has sent HOLD again. The bomb remains unchanged, and there is still no safe basis for Blind to manipulate a wire or control. I relay HOLD and continue waiting.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not touch the bomb; wait for the manual's next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to signal HOLD, so I should not assume a wire operation. The code needs to be explicit and unambiguous for both communicators. I am defining distinct symbols for the five wires and four possible operations, while retaining YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE. Blind must remain hands-off until Mute reports an operation.

``` 
speak(text="Code clarification: YES is thumbs-up, NO thumbs-down, HOLD raised palm, DONE OK. Wire 1 is index-up, wire 2 index-down, wire 3 index-left, wire 4 index-right, wire 5 rightward hand. CUT is victory sign, PRESS is pinch, TURN is crossed fingers, PULL is horns. Mute, report the manual: send HOLD only if it says hold; otherwise send the operation gesture, then the wire gesture if needed, then DONE. Blind, wait.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "👌", "☝", "👇", "👈", "👉", "🫱", "✌", "🤌", "🤞", "🤘"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again sent the established HOLD signal. Since the bomb’s display, light, and wires remain unchanged, I will not infer any operation or ask Blind to touch anything.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD remains in force. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute again signals HOLD. I have no new instruction that authorizes touching or operating any part of the bomb, so Blind must continue to wait.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to signal HOLD, but that may mean either that the manual’s verdict is HOLD or that the current code cannot express the manual’s instruction. I will disambiguate with the existing YES/NO code before authorizing any action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Question: does the manual itself instruct Blind to HOLD and touch nothing? Answer YES with thumbs-up or NO with thumbs-down.")
speak(to="blind", text="Continue HOLD. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
```
